Tourism in Kazakhstan for Arab travellersKazakhstan has become a destination for many Arab travellers looking for new and distinctive experiences, offering a unique trip that satisfies those with a passion for exploration. Before you travel, here are 11 essential pieces of information to help you prepare well and enjoy every moment of your trip. Arab visitors are drawn to Kazakhstan by its picturesque landscape of mountains, lakes and trees, and by its ancient history, which brought together several civilisations that passed through its land, including the Turks and the Mongols, all of whom left traces that bear witness to this in the heart of Kazakhstan’s cities.

Where Is Kazakhstan?

Kazakhstan lies in Central Asia, between Asia and Europe, and is bordered by Russia to the north and China to the east. Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world. Its terrain ranges from mountains and steppes to desert areas and canyons. There are more than 7,000 freshwater and salt lakes, as well as rivers.

Language

Kazakhs speak Kazakh, with Russian as a second language, because Kazakhstan was part of the Soviet Union; only some people speak English.

Currency

The currency of Kazakhstan is the tenge. The exchange rate is 490 tenge to the US dollar, which means it is cheap.

Religion in Kazakhstan

The main religion in Kazakhstan is Islam: Muslims in Kazakhstan make up about 75% of the total population, while Christians in Kazakhstan , together with other religions, account for 15%. That is why the culture of the Kazakh people resembles Arab culture in many ways.

The Capital: Astana

The capital of Kazakhstan is Astana . It is a modern city with many of the architectural masterpieces Kazakhstan is famous for, among them the Bayterek Tower and the Palace of Peace.

Climate and Best Time to Visit

Kazakhstan has a very varied climate: winter is very cold and snowy, while summer brings high temperatures. The time of year you travel will determine the kind of clothing to pack for the trip.

Almaty: The Most Famous City

The most famous city is Almaty, regarded as the largest and finest city in Kazakhstan. It sits at the foot of the Tien Shan mountains and so has the best natural spots in Kazakhstan, as well as being the country’s financial and cultural centre.  Read also: 5 reasons why traveling to Almaty is a great choice

Nature and Tourist Attractions

Kazakhstan combines the culture of the East with the magic of Western nature. It is home to tulips, forests and conifers, on top of its history and culture. Kazakhstan has many natural and historical attractions that appeal to Arab travellers, including the following: Kazakhstan is known for its wonderful tourist cities, such as the capital, Astana, and Almaty, as well as Turkestan, an ancient historic city, and Aktau, on the coast. Halal Food in Kazakhstan

For Arab travellers, the availability of halal food is crucial. As most of Kazakhstan’s people are Muslim, you will find plenty of options and many restaurants serving halal meat, so you can enjoy the unique Kazakh cuisine with peace of mind.

Kazakh Cuisine

Kazakhs love horse meat and use it in all their traditional dishes. It has a strong flavour, different from beef, and it is halal for Muslims. They also use lamb. Kazakhs mainly serve camel milk with meals, and horse-meat soup with onions as a starter. One of the most famous dishes is beshbarmak, made from horse meat with potatoes and pasta. There are also shuzhuk, zhaya and pilaf, and Khan Sirbaz, which is made from lamb.

Medeu Skating Rink

 Kazakhstan is famous for the Medeu rink, the world’s highest outdoor skating rink.

Nightlife and Entertainment

Nightlife in Kazakhstan in cities such as Almaty and Astana is wonderful, with lively, buzzing evenings andfestivals , celebrations, shopping, time spent in restaurants, cafés and clubs, and strolls in the parks.
